title: Jadeja Imitates Kuldeep Yadav's Bowling Action, Leaves Coach Gambhir in Splits
excerpt: The all-rounder's playful mimicry during India's warm-up match against SL XI went viral as the head coach's amused reaction was caught on camera.
body:
• Ravindra Jadeja imitated Kuldeep Yadav's wrist-spin bowling action during India's warm-up match against SL XI ahead of the test series in Sri Lanka
  • Head coach Gautam Gambhir's amused reaction was caught on camera and quickly went viral across social media
  • India begin the two-test series against Sri Lanka on August 15 in Galle, with Jasprit Bumrah ruled out due to a knee injury
  • The playful moment echoes Jadeja's 2017 imitation of a Sri Lankan bowler that left Virat Kohli and Ravi Shastri laughing

A Viral Warm-Up Moment

Ravindra Jadeja provided the lighter side of cricket during India's warm-up match against the SL XI, imitating teammate Kuldeep Yadav's distinctive wrist-spin bowling action and leaving head coach Gautam Gambhir unable to contain his laughter, according to India Today.

https://x.com/Sportskeeda/status/2086080444383293692

The moment, captured during the tour game ahead of India's two-test series in Sri Lanka, quickly gained traction online. News18 reported that the clip of Gambhir's reaction "broke the internet," while NDTV Sports described the coach's response as "priceless."

"Photo: Wikimedia Commons India's Sri Lanka Test Campaign Takes Shape The warm-up match comes at a critical juncture for India's test squad."

Jadeja, a left-arm orthodox spinner, attempted to replicate Kuldeep's chinaman bowling technique — a fundamentally different style that uses wrist rather than finger spin. Both are left-arm bowlers, but the mechanics are worlds apart, making Jadeja's exaggerated attempt all the more entertaining for those watching from the dressing room.

Not His First Performance

This is far from the first time Jadeja has turned the team dressing room into his personal comedy stage. During India's 2017 test series in Sri Lanka, the all-rounder famously imitated the bowling action of Sri Lankan spinner Dilruwan Perera, sending then-captain Virat Kohli and head coach Ravi Shastri into fits of laughter.

The veteran has long been known for lightening the mood in the squad, and his latest antics suggest that dynamic remains intact under Gambhir's coaching tenure.

India's Sri Lanka Test Campaign Takes Shape

The warm-up match comes at a critical juncture for India's test squad. The BCCI confirmed on August 3 that pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah has been ruled out of the series due to a persistent left knee injury sustained during a one-day international against England in Cardiff in July, according to Reuters.

Uncapped fast bowler Auqib Nabi was named as Bumrah's replacement. Nabi took 60 wickets in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy season to help Jammu and Kashmir win their first-ever title, becoming the first cricketer from the region to earn a senior test call-up.

India's squad for the series is captained by Shubman Gill, with KL Rahul as vice-captain. The spin contingent features Jadeja, Kuldeep, and Manav Suthar — a combination built for the turning tracks of Galle and Colombo.

What's Ahead

The first test begins on August 15 at Galle International Cricket Stadium, with the second scheduled from August 23 in Colombo. Without Bumrah, the pace attack will be led by Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna.

Jadeja and Kuldeep's viral warm-up moment may have grabbed the headlines, but attention will soon shift to how India's spin-heavy lineup performs on Sri Lanka's traditionally spin-friendly pitches — starting with the fortress of Galle, where spinners have historically dominated.
